indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2. 2.1.1: Recognize that some events in our environment occur recurrently
indicator.objective: Recognise the importance of some cyclic natural phenomena such as dry and wet seasons

skills.description: Identify the dry season and wet season as cyclic natural events
Describe simple features of the dry season and the wet season
Explain why these seasons are important
Match human activities to the correct season

misconceptions: It rains every single day during the wet season.
There is no water at all during the dry season.
The seasons are the same all over the world.
We only get food during the wet season.
The dry season is bad because everything dies.

questions.stem: What are the two main seasons we experience in Ghana?
hints: One season has a lot of rain.
questions.explanation: Ghana mainly experiences the wet season and the dry season.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think we have four seasons like other countries.

questions.stem: What is the weather like during the wet season?
questions.explanation: The wet season is characterized by rain and cloudy skies.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the wet season is cold like winter.

questions.stem: During the dry season, the weather is usually...
questions.explanation: The dry season is usually sunny and hot with very little rain.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the dry season is cold because it is not raining.

questions.stem: What do farmers need to help their crops grow?
questions.explanation: Farmers need rain during the wet season to water their crops so they can grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think crops only need sunlight.

questions.stem: When do farmers usually plant their seeds?
options: In the middle of the night
hints: The ground needs to be wet.
questions.explanation: Farmers plant their seeds during the wet season so they get enough water to grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think planting happens when it is dry.

questions.stem: Which season has a lot of rain?
questions.explanation: The wet season is the time of the year when it rains a lot.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the wet season with the harmattan.

questions.stem: How does the dry season help farmers?
options: It helps them dry their crops like maize and fish
It helps them plant new seeds
hints: Think about how food is preserved.
questions.explanation: The dry season is useful for drying crops like maize, cocoa, and fish so they can be stored for a long time.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the dry season is only bad for farmers.

questions.stem: When it is raining, what do people use to keep dry?
hints: It opens up like a roof.
You hold it over your head.
questions.explanation: People use umbrellas to protect themselves from the rain.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sunglasses protect from rain.

questions.stem: Do the wet and dry seasons happen once or repeatedly?
hints: Think about the cycle of a year.
questions.explanation: The wet and dry seasons are cyclic events. They happen repeatedly, every year.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seasons only happen once.

questions.stem: What happens to many rivers and streams during the dry season?
options: They dry up or get smaller
hints: There is no rain to fill them.
questions.explanation: During the dry season, rivers and streams often dry up or have less water because there is no rain.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think rivers always have the same amount of water.

questions.stem: Why is the wet season important for animals in the wild?
options: It gives them water to drink and plants to eat
questions.explanation: The wet season provides water for animals to drink and helps plants grow so animals have food to eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think animals do not need rain.

questions.stem: Name one activity people do during the dry season.
hints: Think about what the sun helps us do.
How do we dry our clothes?
questions.explanation: People often dry clothes, food, and harvest crops during the dry season.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name activities that require rain, like planting.

questions.stem: What do we call the season when it rains a lot?
hints: It is the opposite of dry.
questions.explanation: The season with a lot of rain is called the wet season.

questions.stem: Why is the dry season important for drying food like gari and fish?
options: Because there is no rain and the sun is hot
Because the wind blows them away
hints: Think about what makes things dry.
The sun is out all day.
questions.explanation: The dry season is important for drying food because the hot sun and lack of rain help remove moisture, preserving the food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think drying is done in the wet season.

questions.stem: If a farmer plants his seeds in the middle of the dry season, what will likely happen?
options: The seeds will grow very fast
The seeds may not grow and could die
The seeds will turn into stones
hints: The dry season has very little water.
questions.explanation: Seeds need water to grow. Without water from the rains, they may not sprout or they might dry up and die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the hot sun is all a seed needs.

questions.stem: Why do we say the seasons are cyclic?
options: Because they come and go every year in a pattern
Because they are always the same
Because they are caused by cars
hints: Think about a clock going round.
What happens after the wet season? And after the dry?
questions.explanation: Seasons are cyclic because they occur in a repeating pattern year after year.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think 'cyclic' means something is broken.

questions.stem: How does the land usually look during the wet season compared to the dry season?
options: Wet season: green and lush; Dry season: brown and dry
Wet season: brown and dry; Dry season: green and lush
Both seasons look exactly the same
Wet season: covered in snow; Dry season: covered in sand
hints: Plants grow when they get water.
What happens to grass when it is hot and dry?
questions.explanation: During the wet season, plants get plenty of water and look green. In the dry season, they dry up and turn brown.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not observe the difference in vegetation.

questions.stem: Explain why the wet season is important for providing food for the whole country.

criteria.description: States that crops need rain to grow
States that farmers can only get a good harvest if there is enough rain

questions.explanation: The wet season is important because crops need water to grow. Without rain, farmers cannot produce enough food for everyone.

questions.stem: Describe two ways people in your community change their daily activities when the dry season arrives.

criteria.description: Names one valid change (e.g., wearing lighter clothes, using fans, storing water, drying food)

hints: What do you wear when it is hot?
questions.explanation: People adapt to the dry season by wearing light clothing, using fans, storing water, and drying food.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher the names of the two main seasons in Ghana and one thing that happens in each.

criteria.description: Names the wet season and says it rains
Names the dry season and says it is sunny/hot

hints: One starts with W, one starts with D.
questions.explanation: The wet season brings rain, and the dry season brings hot, sunny weather.
